name: financial-data-analyst
tagline: Drop in a spreadsheet, ask a question, watch Claude draw the chart
summary: A Next.js app where you chat with Claude about financial data. You can attach a CSV, text file, PDF or image; the browser turns it into text or base64 and puts it inside your chat message. One server route sends the chat to Claude with a single tool, generate_graph_data. If Claude uses the tool, the server cleans up the chart data and the right-hand panel draws it as a bar, line, area or pie chart.

entities.name: File type sorter
entities.summary: Runs when you pick a file. It sorts the file into image, PDF or 'try it as text', and shows an error toast if reading fails.
entities.details:
- Images (type starts with image/) are kept as base64
- PDFs (application/pdf) have their text pulled out with pdf.js
- Everything else is read as plain text; an empty result is rejected
- Text and PDF results are packed with btoa(encodeURIComponent(text)) and marked isText
- There is no size limit and no allowlist of extensions

guard.rule: Only files that can be read as an image, a PDF's text, or non-empty text get attached
guard.checks: file.type starts with image/, equals application/pdf, or readAsText returns a non-empty string
guard.onFail: A red toast ('PDF parsing failed' or 'Invalid file type') and nothing is attached

entities.name: File readers
entities.summary: Three small helpers that read a file in the browser: as text, as base64, or as PDF text.
entities.details:
- readFileAsText rejects an empty file
- readFileAsBase64 strips the 'data:...;base64,' prefix
- readFileAsPDFText adds a pdf.js script tag from a CDN, walks every page and joins the text
- A new line is added when the y-position jumps more than 5 units

entities.name: File preview chip
entities.summary: Shows the attached file: a small picture for images, or a page icon with the file extension for everything else.
entities.details:
- Large size (with an X to remove) sits above the input box
- Small size sits under your sent message
- Images are shown straight from a data: URL built from the base64
- Long names are cut to 7 letters plus the extension

entities.name: Finance page
entities.summary: The only page. The home route simply shows the finance chat screen: chat on the left, charts on the right.
entities.details:
- app/page.tsx just returns <FinancePage />
- Left card: chat sidebar with model picker and input
- Right card: 'Analysis & Visualizations' with one chart per screen and pagination dots

entities.name: Chat panel
entities.summary: Where you type and send. On send it adds your message and a 'thinking' bubble, then posts the whole chat to /api/finance.
entities.details:
- Does nothing if the box is empty and no file is attached
- Text files are decoded and pasted into the message as 'File contents of <name>'
- Images become an image block plus a text block
- Every earlier message (and its file) is re-sent on every turn
- On success the thinking bubble is replaced with the reply and chart; on error with an apology

entities.name: Chat memory
entities.summary: React state that holds every message (with its file and chart) plus the file waiting to be sent.
entities.details:
- messages: the full history; lives only in the browser tab
- currentUpload: the attached file until the next send
- A message may carry chartData, which puts it in the chart panel
- Refreshing the page wipes everything

entities.name: Model list
entities.summary: The three Claude models you can pick from the dropdown. The chosen id is sent with each request.
entities.details:
- Claude 3 Haiku, Claude 4.5 Haiku, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
- Default is claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620
- The server does not check the id against this list

entities.name: POST /api/finance
entities.summary: The one server route. It reads the chat and model from the request and copies the messages for Claude.
entities.details:
- Runs on the edge runtime
- Reads { messages, fileData, model } from the JSON body
- Has a fileData branch, but the current page never sends fileData (files are already inside messages)
- Sends back { content, hasToolUse, toolUse, chartData }

entities.name: Request check
entities.summary: Stops the request early if there is no messages array or no model.
entities.details:
- messages must exist and be an array
- model must be set (any string is accepted)
- Fails with HTTP 400 and a JSON error

guard.rule: A request must carry a chat history and a model
guard.onFail: HTTP 400 'Messages array is required' or 'Model selection is required'

entities.name: Chart data check
entities.summary: Looks at what Claude put into the tool call, checks the basics, reshapes pie data and paints each series a color.
entities.details:
- Throws if chartType is missing or data is not an array
- Pie: rows are rebuilt as { segment, value } using xAxisKey and the first chartConfig key
- Each chartConfig key gets a color hsl(var(--chart-1)), --chart-2, ... in order
- The chartType value itself is not checked against the six allowed names

guard.rule: Tool output must look like a chart before it is sent to the browser
guard.checks: chartData.chartType is set and chartData.data is an array
guard.onFail: Throws 'Invalid chart data structure', which becomes an HTTP 500

entities.name: Error catcher
entities.summary: The big catch at the end of the route. It turns any thrown error into a JSON error response.
entities.details:
- Anthropic API errors return their own status code
- The AuthenticationError branch is never reached, because APIError is checked first and covers it
- Anything else becomes HTTP 500 with the error message

guard.rule: No error escapes the route without a JSON answer
guard.checks: error instanceof Anthropic.APIError, then AuthenticationError, else generic
guard.onFail: Returns { error, details } with the API status, 401, or 500

entities.name: The Analyst
entities.summary: Claude, called once per message with the chart tool and a long system prompt. It either answers in text, calls the chart tool, or both.
entities.details:
- One call to messages.create, no loop and no tool_result sent back
- max_tokens 4096, temperature 0.7
- tool_choice auto: Claude decides if a chart is needed
- Told never to mention that it is using the tool

agent.role: Reads financial data and answers with insight and, when useful, a chart spec

entities.name: generate_graph_data tool
entities.summary: The only tool Claude has. It is not code that runs; its input is the chart spec the app draws.
entities.details:
- chartType: bar, multiBar, line, pie, area or stackedArea
- config: title and description required; trend, footer, totalLabel, xAxisKey optional
- data: array of rows with any keys
- chartConfig: one entry per series, each with a label

entities.name: Analyst system prompt
entities.summary: Tells Claude it is a financial chart expert, when to use each chart type, and shows example data shapes.
entities.details:
- Lists the six chart types with use cases
- Gives example data for time series, multi-bar and pie
- Says: use real data, add trend and footer, never announce the tool

source.anchor: You are a financial data visualization expert.

entities.name: Anthropic API
entities.summary: Claude's home. The route builds one Anthropic client from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.
entities.details:
- Key is read once at module load
- The browser never sees the key; it only talks to /api/finance

entities.name: Chart renderer
entities.summary: Picks a chart component by chartType and draws it with Recharts inside a card with title, trend and footer.
entities.details:
- bar draws only the first chartConfig key
- multiBar, line, area, stackedArea draw one series per chartConfig key
- pie adds up 'value' for the number in the middle
- Unknown chartType returns null (an empty slot)
- Wrapped in SafeChartRenderer, whose try/catch cannot catch errors thrown inside the chart

quests.title: The spreadsheet surprise
quests.prompt: You attach an Excel file (budget.xlsx). What does the upload code do with it?
options: Rejects it because only CSV is allowed
Reads its raw bytes as text and attaches that
Sends it to Claude as an image
quests.explain: Anything that is not image/* or application/pdf goes to readFileAsText. A .xlsx gives non-empty garbled text, so it passes and is attached.

options: Never: files are already pasted into messages
quests.explain: handleSubmit sends only { messages, model }. Files are inlined into message content, so fileData is always undefined.

quests.explain: chart-check only checks that chartType is set. ChartRenderer's switch falls to default and returns null.

quests.explain: processToolResponse rewrites chartConfig, giving each key hsl(var(--chart-N)) in order.

cracks.title: Every file is re-sent on every turn, with no size limit
cracks.hint: What happens to the CSV you attached three messages ago?
cracks.finding: handleSubmit maps over all past messages and pastes each file's full text (or base64 image) back in every time. Nothing limits file size, so a big CSV is sent again and again until the request hits Claude's context limit and fails.
cracks.suggestion: Check file size on pick, and send each file once (or summarize old files) instead of re-inlining all history.
decoys: The CSV is parsed twice on the server
The model id is not sent with the request

cracks.title: Pie values can vanish
cracks.hint: Which key does the pie use for value, and what if it is 0?
cracks.finding: Pie rows take value from the first chartConfig key, else item.value. If that key is not a data column (the prompt's own example uses 'equities' while rows use 'value') and rows use another name like 'amount', value is undefined and the center total becomes NaN. A real 0 also falls through the || check.
cracks.suggestion: Use config.xAxisKey plus an explicit value key, check it exists in the rows, and use ?? instead of ||.
decoys: Pie colors repeat after two slices

cracks.title: The safety net has a hole
cracks.hint: Can a try/catch around JSX catch an error that happens later, while React draws?
cracks.finding: SafeChartRenderer wraps <ChartRenderer/> in try/catch, but it only builds the element; child render errors happen later and are not caught. A malformed spec can crash the whole page instead of showing 'Error rendering chart'.
cracks.suggestion: Use a React error boundary (class component or react-error-boundary) around each chart.
decoys: Charts are drawn before the data arrives
The chart list uses the index as key

cracks.title: Failed PDF still says 'success'
cracks.hint: Does an early return skip the finally block?
cracks.finding: When PDF parsing fails the code shows 'PDF parsing failed' and returns, but the finally block still runs and, because a loading toast exists for PDFs, shows 'PDF Processed: Text extracted successfully'.
cracks.suggestion: Track success in a flag and only show the success toast when the text was extracted.

Images also show the PDF toast
